activity_context.topic_title: The Cartesian Equation of a Plane

feedback.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,-2,5)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
${\begin{aligned}x=4+3t \\ y=1-4t \\ z=-3-2t\end{aligned}.$

{{field-1}}
$x\,-4y\,-\,$ 
{{field-2}} $z\,-$
{{field-3}}$\,=0$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨1,-2,5⟩.$ From the parametrical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨3,-4,-2⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨3,-4,-2⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,-2⟩ & =⟨1,-2,5⟩\cdot ⟨3,-4,-2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,-2⟩ & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,-4,-2⟩ & =1 \\ 3x-4y-2z & =1 \\ 3x-4y-2z-1 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
